cvEn:
Yaakov Mahbub, the youngest son of Shlomo and Ada, was born on 27 Tishrei 5711 (7 October 1950) in Tel Aviv. He began his schooling at the Ussishkin school and continued at Kibbutz Gesher, where he developed a close bond with his friends and a love of work. He loved the kibbutz landscape and its surroundings and spent much time walking through the area.

After leaving the kibbutz, he studied at the "Einot" agricultural high school near Ness Ziona. By the time he arrived there, he already had agricultural and mechanical knowledge. Even as a young man he operated agricultural equipment, and thanks to this knowledge he was entrusted with positions of responsibility. He enjoyed photography as a hobby, and he was a sociable person, friendly and well liked by his comrades. They recall that he was the class comedian, and he had a great talent for pantomime.

Yaakov was drafted into the IDF in November 1968. After completing basic training, he was sent to a course for machine-gun crews, but he did not complete it, as he was sent to a signals course and served as a signaler until his last day. He fell on 20 Shevat 5730 (27 January 1970) in the Suez area. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery at Kiryat Shaul.
